item.title: Return Oriented Programming
item.description:
ROP Exploit with Arbitrary Write to .bss and Reverse Shell via system()

Description: This repository contains a Return-Oriented Programming (ROP) exploit targeting a 64-bit Linux binary vulnerable to buffer overflow. The exploit performs an arbitrary write to the .bss section to inject a reverse shell command, which is then executed using system(). The goal is to gain a remote shell on the target system.

item.title: Welcome to My Cybersecurity Blog
item.description:
👋 Hello and Welcome!

I’m Talen Neil Serrao, a Cybersecurity and Ethical Hacking graduate from Coventry University 🇬🇧, awarded First Class Honours.
I’m currently studying for an MSc in Cyber Security Engineering at the University of Warwick, and this website is a space where I share what I’m learning, building, and exploring in cybersecurity.

item.title: Building a Simple SHA-256 Hash Cracker in Python
item.description:
Introduction

As part of my journey in cybersecurity and ethical hacking, I built a simple SHA-256 hash cracking tool using Python. The goal of this project was not to break real systems, but to understand how password hashing works, how attackers misuse weak passwords, and why strong password policies and salting are critical in modern security.
